rationale: The grader candidate is suitable for Harbor packaging. (1) Scope: all five scientific endpoints of the original notebook are preserved in one task — three recorded append-only exports (core_ca, mass_weighted, resid_weighted) plus two endpoints recovered by policy-permitted faithful recomputation of the unchanged original calls at the required state (fresh Universes, frame 0), with construction-time determinism evidence and byte-identical copies of the recorded reference exports; plots are visualization-only and correctly excluded. (2) Source fidelity of the public contract: the two pivotal methodology claims were verified directly in the pinned MDAnalysis 2.11.0 sdist — rms.py _prepare (lines 691-707) confirms weights='mass' also mass-weights groupselections, so the public question's mass-weighted domain-column definition matches the executed code rather than the source narrative the code contradicts; the group-selection rule (center=False, superposition=False against raw un-recentered reference group coordinates after the global fit) matches rms.py lines 733-741 and 818-824; the backbone definition (names N/CA/C/O in protein residues, OT* excluded) matches selection.py BackboneSelection; both validated implementations (the oracle and the independently executed NumPy/SVD Kabsch solution, which share only the file readers) agree within tolerance per the executed alternative control. (3) Contract vs implementation: the corrected check descriptions accurately describe the unchanged grader code — exact parsed-float cross-file Time identity (no tolerance in the vals-set comparison; 1e-9 only per-file against the reference), and csv.reader unquoting with identical parsed-content rules for quoted fields; neither correction weakens a tolerance or removes an obligation. The disclosed tolerance model (max(3e-6 Å, 1e-9·|r|)) is not generous toward any wrong method probed or plausible (wrong weights, per-domain refit, cross-file/CORE quantity confusion, truncation, duplication, nan/inf, tolerance boundary all fail, as executed). (4) Controls: 26/26 executed as expected on the current candidate hash, including reference, recomputed, alternative, empty, misplaced (nested outputs/ rejected, matching the addendum path rules) and five per-file missing controls; probe scripts, names, kinds and focus values are unchanged from initial_probes — only rationales/check_ids were corrected, and each listed check genuinely fails per the executed reports. The reader-convention dependence of the Time (ns) column is honestly disclosed in both question and addendum and is deterministic in the pinned environment (ts.time = (frame + istart/nsavc) · dt, verified in DCD.py), consistent with the policy that broad implementation independence is not promised.

source_coverage.rationale: The original converted source contains five scientific terminal results: (1) the open-vs-closed scalar backbone RMSD, (2) the Universe multi-selection Backbone/CORE/LID/NMP RMSD, (3) the AtomGroup CORE alpha-carbon RMSD, (4) the mass-weighted RMSD table, and (5) the resid-weighted RMSD table. The earlier preparation inventory exported only (3)-(5); the construction stage recovered (1) and (2) under the endpoint_recovery policy by rerunning the unchanged original calls (rms.rmsd with center=True/superposition=True; rms.RMSD(u, u, select='backbone', groupselections=[CORE, LID, NMP], ref_frame=0)) on the same pinned PSF/DCD inputs at the required state (fresh Universe at frame 0), with separate provenance, two-run determinism verification, and the recorded reference exports copied verbatim. Both earlier exclusion reasons ('unnamed expression', 'overwritten by later analysis') are exactly the grounds the recovery policy permits faithful recomputation for. The pandas line plots contain no numerical content beyond the exported DataFrames and are visualization-only. The input claims (derived from PDB 1AKE/4AKE, 98 frames, 3341 protein-only atoms, mass/resid metadata in the PSF) are corroborated by the MDAnalysisTests reference material and the pinned source. The public contract defines the executed quantities per the pinned MDAnalysis 2.11.0 semantics (verified against analysis/rms.py and core/selection.py), including the mass-weighted group selections that the source narrative mislabels as unweighted. No eligible scientific branch is missing and no unsupported claim survives in the public question.
